newsitem.title: LIECHTENSTEIN: Tiny Liechtenstein reports first "mad cat" case.
newsitem.headline: Tiny Liechtenstein reports first "mad cat" case.

text.p: The small Alpine principality of Liechtenstein on Thursday reported its first case of a cat suffering from the feline equivalent of mad cow disease.

The government veterinary office said the nine-year-old male cat was put to sleep after being diagnosed with Feline Spongiform Encephalopathy (FSE), which destroys the brain in the same way as the bovine version does in cows.
"The cause of FSE in the Liechtenstein cat can probably be traced to feeding it years ago with raw or underheated brain or spinal cord tissue from cattle," a statement said.
It said this kind of material was no longer used in pet food.
"There is no danger of infection for people," the veterinary office added.
